title: This is Your Brain on Ads

sentences.en: There are so many universals in the human experience.
sentences.zh: 人类体验中有那么多的普遍性。

sentences.en: They drive us as much as they did humans a hundred, a thousand, or even a hundred thousand years ago.
sentences.zh: 它们驱使着我们，就像一百年前、一千年前，甚至十万年前驱使人类一样。

sentences.en: But there are also experiences that feel unique to our current moment,
sentences.zh: 但也有一些体验让我们觉得是当今时代独有的，

sentences.en: that only modern humans have encountered.
sentences.zh: 是现代人类才遇到过的。

sentences.en: Among them, the many competing forces desperately seeking our attention.
sentences.zh: 在这些体验中，有许多争夺我们注意力的竞争力量。

sentences.en: The social media and news apps pushing alerts to our phones.
sentences.zh: 将警报推送到我们手机上的社交媒体和新闻应用程序。

sentences.en: The streaming TV services, and yes, podcasts, offering us endless opportunities to binge our favorite shows.
sentences.zh: 流媒体电视服务，还有播客，为我们提供了无尽的机会来疯狂追看我们喜爱的节目。

sentences.en: All this clamoring for our attention can be exhausting.
sentences.zh: 所有这些对我们注意力的呐喊可能会让人筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: It reminded us of an episode we did a little while back about how our attention is being constantly harvested and hijacked.
sentences.zh: 这让我们想起不久前做过的一期节目，关于我们的注意力是如何被不断收割和劫持的。

sentences.en: Esther Bly grew up with a mom who kept her kitchen free from food coloring and high-fructose corn syrup.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特·布莱的母亲对她要求严格，厨房里没有人工色素和高果糖玉米糖浆。

sentences.en: Esther's lunchbox was subject to the same rules.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特的午餐盒也遵循同样的规则。

sentences.en: So I would have snap peas, I would have an orange.
sentences.zh: 所以我会有糖豌豆，我会有橙子。

sentences.en: Sometimes it would be leftovers, and one maybe like gummy snack, but it would only be like health gummy.
sentences.zh: 有时会是剩菜，可能还有一个软糖零食，但那也只会是健康的软糖。

sentences.en: Of course, Esther craved the processed snacks and cereals that her classmates were eating.
sentences.zh: 当然，埃丝特渴望她的同学们正在吃的加工零食和谷物食品。
电视广告激发了她的渴望。

sentences.en: One of her favorites was for Trix yogurt.
sentences.zh: 她最喜欢的广告之一是关于崔克斯酸奶的。

sentences.en: Trix rabbit is inside this costume.
sentences.zh: 崔克斯兔子就在这套服装里面。

sentences.en: And he starts describing all the wonderful fruits that, you know, aren't real, but they act like they're real.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始描述所有那些你知道的、不是真的，但它们表现得像真的美妙水果。
草莓、香蕉狂欢、树莓、彩虹。

sentences.en: As the kids take a bite, they start to turn to color.
sentences.zh: 当孩子们咬上一口时，他们开始变色。

sentences.en: And at the very end, everything's like technicolor.
sentences.zh: 而在最后，一切就像全彩色一样。

sentences.en: Now, Trix yogurt, of course, was banned from the Bly family fridge because it had artificial flavors and food colorings.
sentences.zh: 当然，崔克斯酸奶被布莱一家的冰箱拒之门外，因为它有人工香料和食用色素。

sentences.en: But at breakfast time, Esther says her mom allowed her one solitary, sugary exception.
sentences.zh: 但埃丝特说，在早餐时间，她妈妈允许她有一个单独的、含糖的特例。

sentences.en: So I wasn't encouraged to have sugary cereals unless possibly her or my father had had them growing up.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不被鼓励吃含糖麦片，除非她或我父亲在成长过程中吃过。

sentences.en: So it was kind of that nostalgic allowance.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像那种带有怀旧色彩的放纵。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, how advertisers, tech companies, and influencers exploit this nostalgia allowance and other aspects of human behavior to capture our attention.
sentences.zh: 今天是“隐性大脑”节目，我们将探讨广告商、科技公司和网红如何利用这种怀旧宽容以及人类行为的其他方面来吸引我们的注意力。

sentences.en: Esther's parents let her have frosted flakes and lucky charms for breakfast because they ate frosted flakes and lucky charms for breakfast when they were kids.
sentences.zh: 埃丝特的父母让她吃霜糖片和幸运麦片作为早餐，因为他们小时候就吃霜糖片和幸运麦片当早餐。

sentences.en: If you think about it, parents love to have their kids experience the same wonderful things that they did.
sentences.zh: 如果你仔细想想，父母很喜欢让他们的孩子体验他们曾经经历过的那些美妙事情。
这位是玛丽·布鲁克斯教授。

sentences.en: I work at the Eller College of Management.
sentences.zh: 我在埃勒管理学院工作。

sentences.en: And I'm interested in the psychology of advertising effects.
sentences.zh: 我对广告效果的心理学很感兴趣。

sentences.en: Mary says it isn't just the taste and smell of sugary cereals that cement memories in our minds.
sentences.zh: 玛丽说，在我们的脑海中巩固记忆的，不仅仅是含糖麦片的味道和气味。

sentences.en: It's the advertising that sells those products.
sentences.zh: 是推销这些产品的广告。

sentences.en: For a six- or seven-year-old, commercials with fun mascots like Lucky the Leprechaun and Tony the Tiger can be really powerful.
sentences.zh: 对于六七岁的孩子来说，带有幸运小妖精和托尼老虎等有趣吉祥物的广告可能会非常震撼。

sentences.en: Children are vulnerable to messages that are fun and sound good and you can sing and they have fun characters because their minds are just so open to all of that.
sentences.zh: 孩子们很容易受到那些有趣、听起来不错、你可以跟着唱并且有有趣角色的信息的吸引，因为他们的心灵对这一切都是敞开的。
他们对一切都持开放态度。
小孩子并不持怀疑态度。

sentences.en: They don't listen to commercials with cute rabbits and think, a multi-billion dollar company is trying to influence me.
sentences.zh: 他们不会听着带有可爱兔子的广告想，一个价值数十亿美元的公司正试图影响我。

sentences.en: Of course, at a certain point, this changes and kids start to think of commercials as commercials.
sentences.zh: 当然，到了某个时候，这种情况会发生变化，孩子们开始把广告看作是广告。

sentences.en: Presumably, you have some ideas on when the window opens and closes in terms of our vulnerability or impressionability.
sentences.zh: 据推测，在我们的脆弱性或易受影响性方面，对于这个窗口期何时开启和关闭，你有一些看法。

sentences.en: What does that window look like?
sentences.zh: 那个窗口期是什么样的？

sentences.en: The research says, and I'm not sure I believe it, that the vulnerability ends around 13 in terms of your cognitive ability,
sentences.zh: 研究表明——虽然我不确定我是否相信——就认知能力而言，这种脆弱性在大约13岁时结束，

sentences.en: meaning children's understanding of what advertising is and how it works and that they should not be open to it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着孩子们理解什么是广告、它是如何运作的，以及他们不应该轻易受到它的影响。
你应该进行批判性思考。

sentences.en: And they're able to, at the same time they're hearing it, question it.
sentences.zh: 他们能够在听到它的同时对其提出质疑。
这里有一个有趣的问题。

sentences.en: What happens to those messages that we heard when we were small?
sentences.zh: 我们小时候听到那些信息会怎么样？

sentences.en: Do our grown-up minds question them?
sentences.zh: 我们成年后的思维会去质疑它们吗？

sentences.en: To answer that question, Mary teamed up with two colleagues.
sentences.zh: 为了回答这个问题，玛丽与两位同事合作。

sentences.en: Paul Connell at Stony Brook University and one of my professor colleagues here.
sentences.zh: 斯托尼布鲁克大学的保罗·康奈尔和我在这里的一位教授同事。
他的名字叫杰斯帕·尼尔森。

sentences.en: And the trio arranged a series of studies to look at how adults viewed cereal products.
sentences.zh: 这三个人安排了一系列研究，来观察成年人如何看待麦片产品。

sentences.en: First thing we wanted to do is to establish that we can tie people's beliefs about the nutritiousness of a product with their exposure to that product when they were children.
sentences.zh: 我们想做的第一件事是证明，我们可以将人们对产品营养价值的看法与他们童年时期对该产品的接触联系起来。

sentences.en: They gathered a sample of people in the United Kingdom and asked them to rate the healthfulness of a chocolate-puffed rice cereal called Cocoa Pops.
sentences.zh: 他们在英国收集了样本，并要求他们评价一种名为“可可波波”的巧克力膨化大米麦片的健康程度。

sentences.en: For cereal connoisseurs, Cocoa Pops are not to be confused with the Cocoa Pops that American listeners may have grown up eating.
sentences.zh: 对于麦片行家来说，可可波波不应该与美国听众可能从小吃到大的可可波波混淆。

sentences.en: The Cocoa Pops mascot is a smiling monkey wearing a blue baseball cap.
sentences.zh: 可可波波的吉祥物是一只戴着蓝色棒球帽的微笑猴子。

sentences.en: Some people in the study only learned about Cocoa Pops when they were adults.
sentences.zh: 研究中的一些人直到成年才了解可可波波。

sentences.en: Others grew up eating the cereal and had seen commercials for it when they were small kids.
sentences.zh: 其他人则是从小吃这种麦片长大，并且在他们很小的时候就看过它的广告。

sentences.en: Those people rated as much more nutritious.
sentences.zh: 这些人对其营养价值的评价要高得多。

sentences.en: So everyone else has a more accurate rating of how nutritious this is,
sentences.zh: 所以其他所有人对这东西有多营养都有更准确的评价，

sentences.en: except for the people who saw it as a child and who have feelings of liking and warmth towards the Cocoa Monkey.
sentences.zh: 除了那些在小时候看过它，并且对可可猴有好感和温情的人。

sentences.en: Only Kemal Cocoa Pops has Cocoa's magic secret, so it looks and tastes magic.
sentences.zh: 只有卡迈尔可可波波拥有可可的魔法秘密，所以它看起来和尝起来都有魔力。

sentences.en: And part of a nutritious breakfast, I'd rather have a...
sentences.zh: 作为营养早餐的一部分，我宁愿吃一个……
你注意到那句台词了吗？

sentences.en: Cereal commercials often use language like this.
sentences.zh: 麦片广告经常使用这样的语言。

sentences.en: Now, if you're a skeptical adult, you might guess that a cereal with cocoa or marshmallows in the ingredients is not your healthiest option.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你是一个持怀疑态度的成年人，你可能会猜到含有可可或棉花糖成分的麦片并不是你最健康的的选择。

sentences.en: But if you're a kid, a nutritious breakfast sounds pretty good.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是个孩子，营养早餐听起来相当不错。

sentences.en: So shouldn't your grown-up brain correct for the mistakes of your impressionable brain when you were a kid?
sentences.zh: 那么，你成年后的大脑难道不应该纠正你小时候那个易受影响的大脑所犯的错误吗？

sentences.en: Well, to me, one of the scary things is adults don't correct for it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对我来说，可怕的事情之一就是成年人不会去纠正它。

sentences.en: They don't later on say, you know, I have these memories from when I was a child and, you know, they're wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们后来不会说，你知道，我有这些来自童年的记忆，而且，你知道，它们是错的。
我真的应该重新考虑一下。

sentences.en: So in our later studies, that's what we actually checked, is would people, if we helped them by reminding them of health, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以在我们后来的研究中，我们实际检验的正是这一点：如果我们通过提醒他们健康，例如，

sentences.en: or reminding them of children's vulnerability to advertising, that if we were to do that, would they then correct these biases?
sentences.zh: 或者提醒他们儿童对广告的脆弱性来帮助他们，如果我们这样做，他们会纠正这些偏见吗？

sentences.en: And what we found, again, is that the people who felt that emotion towards these characters did not correct for it.
sentences.zh: 我们再次发现的是，对这些角色产生这种情感的人并没有对其进行纠正。

sentences.en: So shouldn't the average adult be able to say, look, I liked the mascot when I was a child, but I'm not a child anymore.
sentences.zh: 所以普通成年人难道不应该能够说，听着，我小时候喜欢这个吉祥物，但我已经不是小孩子了。

sentences.en: I'm too old now to believe in childish things, so I should just set it aside.
sentences.zh: 我现在太老了，不应该相信幼稚的事情，所以我应该把它放在一边。

sentences.en: I think if you ask most adults, do you want to behave childishly, they will say no.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你问大多数成年人，你想表现得幼稚吗，他们会说不。

sentences.en: Why is this effect still persisting?
sentences.zh: 为什么这种效应仍在持续？

sentences.en: Why does the effects of what we hear in childhood stay in our minds if we want to leave those behind in a way?
sentences.zh: 如果我们某种程度上想把它们抛在脑后，为什么我们在童年听到的话的影响会留在我们的脑海里？

sentences.en: Well, you'd have to really want to leave those behind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你必须真的想要把它们抛在脑后才行。

sentences.en: So I think that's an individual difference.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这是一种个体差异。

sentences.en: Some people do move away from the love of the things they had as kids.
sentences.zh: 有些人确实不再留恋他们小时候拥有的东西。

sentences.en: But if you think about it, parents love to have their kids experience the same wonderful things that they did,
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想，父母很喜欢让他们的孩子体验他们曾经经历过的那些美妙事情，

sentences.en: which is why parents love to take their kids to Disney, and they love to share with them the toys that they had.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么父母喜欢带孩子去迪士尼，喜欢和他们分享他们自己曾拥有的玩具。

sentences.en: And I think that they still love these things.
sentences.zh: 我想他们仍然喜爱这些东西。

sentences.en: Her health-conscious parents made an exception for Frosted Flakes because they grew up with Tony the Tiger,
sentences.zh: 她注重健康的父母破例为她买了霜糖片，因为他们是伴随着老虎托尼长大的，

sentences.en: and not just on the cereal box.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是在麦片盒上。

sentences.en: Tony the Tiger, my grandma, still kept the trash can.
sentences.zh: 老虎托尼，我奶奶，一直留着那个垃圾桶。

sentences.en: So we have this very old Kellogg trash can with Tony the Tiger, one of his very first designs from the 60s, 70s.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一个非常古老的家乐氏垃圾桶，上面有老虎托尼，这是他在60年代、70年代最早的设计之一。

sentences.en: Cereal mascots appear to have incredible power.
sentences.zh: 麦片吉祥物似乎拥有不可思议的力量。

sentences.en: Esther told us about the Trix yogurt ad that stuck with her, but she also remembers specific ads for Froot Loops.
sentences.zh: 埃斯特向我们讲述了那个让她印象深刻的崔克斯酸奶广告，但她也记得针对果味圈的特定广告。

sentences.en: Yeah, I really liked Sam the Toucan because he would go and explore.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真的很喜欢大嘴鸟萨姆，因为他会去探索。

sentences.en: There's these dancing Oreo figures, and it reminded me of the Flubber ad.
sentences.zh: 有这些跳舞的奥利奥人物，这让我想起了《弗莱伯》的广告。

sentences.en: She's never even tried the Oreo one, but she still feels a kind of strange fondness for it.
sentences.zh: 她甚至从未尝过奥利奥的那款，但她对它依然有一种奇怪的喜爱之情。

sentences.en: For kids, telling a story is very easy to do, especially when you have mascot involvement.
sentences.zh: 对于孩子们来说，讲故事是一件非常容易做到的事情，特别是当有吉祥物参与时。

sentences.en: In 2016, based in part on research studies like the one Mary Brooks conducted,
sentences.zh: 2016年，部分基于像玛丽·布鲁克斯所进行的那些研究，

sentences.en: the country of Chile banned mascots from all product packaging
sentences.zh: 智利共和国禁止在所有产品包装上使用吉祥物，

sentences.en: and launched a media campaign to educate people about healthier foods.
sentences.zh: 并发起了一场媒体运动，向人们普及更健康食品的知识。

sentences.en: Mascots have been removed from all sorts of products, from chips to cereals.
sentences.zh: 吉祥物已从从薯片到麦片的各种产品中被移除。

sentences.en: Some foods also have a black sticker slapped on them with labels like alto and calorías, high in calories,
sentences.zh: 有些食品还贴上了黑色的标签，上面写着“高热量”等字样，

sentences.en: or alto and azucariz, high in sugar.
I asked Mary if she thinks it'll work.
sentences.zh: 我问玛丽她认为这管不管用。

sentences.en: Based on my research, I would be fully supportive of that effort.
sentences.zh: 根据我的研究，我会全力支持这项工作。

sentences.en: If they do it for 10 years and it doesn't work, well, then we should go back to the way it is.
sentences.zh: 如果他们坚持10年而不管用，好吧，那我们就应该回到原来的样子。

sentences.en: But I think it will work.
I just don't think you're going to see the result for a long time,
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得你不会在短时间内看到结果，

sentences.en: because these effects build up over a long time.
sentences.zh: 因为这些影响是在很长一段时间内积累起来的。

sentences.en: Mary herself remembers commercials from her childhood that have stuck with her for several decades.
sentences.zh: 玛丽自己还记得她童年时期的广告，这些广告在她脑海中留存了几十年。

sentences.en: I have a memory of walking to elementary school with my friends, singing the Winston jingle.
sentences.zh: 我记得和朋友们一起步行去小学，唱着温斯顿的广告歌。

sentences.en: That's why more people smoke Winston than any other filter cigarette.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么抽温斯顿的人比抽任何其他过滤嘴香烟的人都多。

sentences.en: When I changed to Winston, I changed for good,
sentences.zh: 当我换成温斯顿，我一去不回头，

sentences.en: because I got good taste like I knew I would.
sentences.zh: 因为我得到了如我所知的好味道。

sentences.en: Winston tastes good like it should.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿味道好，本该如此。

sentences.en: Changed to Winston and changed for good,
sentences.zh: 换成温斯顿，一去不回头，

sentences.en: because Winston tastes good like a cigarette should.
sentences.zh: 因为温斯顿味道好，就像香烟本来应该的那样。
这是一个令人不安的画面。

sentences.en: Elementary schoolers singing a song about the virtues of smoking.
sentences.zh: 小学生们唱着一首歌颂吸烟优点的歌。

sentences.en: You might think that as a society,
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为作为一个社会，

sentences.en: we would decide to expose our children to fewer advertisements.
sentences.zh: 我们会决定让我们的孩子接触更少的广告。

sentences.en: But in fact, as a school district in California shows,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，正如加利福尼亚州的一个学区所展示的那样，

sentences.en: we might be going in exactly the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 我们可能正朝着完全相反的方向前进。

sentences.en: Back in 2012, the Twin Rivers Unified School District was strapped for cash.
sentences.zh: 早在2012年，双河联合学区资金短缺。

sentences.en: Benefactors stepped in and offered to help.
sentences.zh: 慈善家们介入并提供帮助。

sentences.en: But there was one small catch.
sentences.zh: 但有一个小小的附加条件。

sentences.en: The benefactors wanted something in exchange.
sentences.zh: 慈善家们想要一些回报。

sentences.en: Here's Columbia University researcher Tim Wu.
sentences.zh: 这位是哥伦比亚大学研究员蒂姆·吴。

sentences.en: They wanted nothing less than the attention of the students.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的正是学生的注意力。

sentences.en: So they proposed that the school could have all,
sentences.zh: 所以他们提议学校可以拥有所有，

sentences.en: not all the money it wants, but great riches
sentences.zh: 不是它想要的全部资金，而是巨大的财富。

sentences.en: if it only agreed to subject its students to advertising,
sentences.zh: 如果它仅仅同意让学生们接触广告，

sentences.en: you know, covering the lockers with ads,
sentences.zh: 比如说，在储物柜上贴满广告，

sentences.en: some in-class advertisements, ads in the cafeteria.
sentences.zh: 课堂上穿插一些广告，餐厅里也有广告。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's part of a big trend
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这也是一大趋势的一部分，

sentences.en: where schools that are strapped for cash
have occasionally turned to their captive audiences,
sentences.zh: 偶尔会转向他们手头现成的受众，

sentences.en: After the break, Tim Wu pulls back the curtain
